items.stem: What does `typeof null` evaluate to in JavaScript?

options.rationale: Correct: a long-standing language quirk - typeof null returns "object".
There is no "null" string result from typeof; null is not its own typeof tag.
typeof undefined is "undefined"; null is a distinct value.
null is not a boolean; it is the intentional absence of an object value.

items.explanation: Correct: a long-standing language quirk - typeof null returns "object".

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Promises are correct?

options.text: A promise can settle (resolve or reject) only once
options.rationale: Correct: once settled a promise's state is immutable.

options.text: async/await is built on top of promises
options.rationale: Correct: await pauses on a promise and resumes with its settled value.

options.text: A rejected promise without a handler is always caught by a surrounding try/catch
options.rationale: Only an awaited (or .catch-chained) promise is caught; a bare rejected promise is not.

options.text: Promise.all resolves as soon as the first input promise resolves
options.rationale: That describes Promise.race; Promise.all waits for all to resolve (or any to reject).

items.explanation: Correct: once settled a promise's state is immutable.

items.stem: A loop uses `var i` and registers a callback referencing `i`. All callbacks log the same final value. What is the BEST fix?

options.text: Declare the loop counter with let instead of var
options.rationale: Correct: let creates a fresh binding per iteration, so each callback captures its own value.

options.text: Move the callback outside the loop
options.rationale: That changes behaviour and does not give per-iteration values.

options.text: Use == instead of === in the comparison
options.rationale: Equality operators are unrelated to closure binding.

options.text: Add 'use strict' at the top of the file
options.rationale: Strict mode does not change var's function-level scoping here.

items.explanation: Correct: let creates a fresh binding per iteration, so each callback captures its own value.
